Direct control district is a regulatory tool established through the Planning and Development Act 2007.

It is a tool used specifically for the development that is required to be highly regulated or to facilitate unique development proposals which may not be facilitated through existing zoning districts or controls within the zoning by law.
A direct control district specifies the permitted uses of land, buildings, structures, services, landscaping and other related matters as required.
They may also allow for the developer and municipality to enter into a development agreement based on a concept plan to negotiate aspects of the details, design and uses of a development.
The official community plan section J5.2 speaks the policy pertaining to direct control district uses as a tool within the city.

Direct control district 3 or DCD-3 was established by Council in October 2000. The area was established as a DCD to ensure a high degree of site design and architectural features which are complementary to the setting and architecture of the University of Saskatchewan.
And to permit city council to exercise control over the eventual timing, site design, access, egress, landscaping, lighting and other development standards of each phase of development.
DCD-3 was originally established as a three-phase development.

However, in 2011, phase 4 was established and following phase 5 in 2013 to allow for a full build-out of the total 28.42 hectares or 70.24 acres of the pressing cross and crossing regional commercial area.
The purpose of DCD-3 is to create for a site of a class of retail land in Saskatchewan, located on land owned by the University of Saskatchewan in the vicinity of Circle and Outreach.
The primary focus of the retail class is to accommodate large format or big box retail stores which are not readily accommodated in other standard commercial areas of Saskatchewan.
The applicant is proposing an amendment to the current DCD-3 concept plan to facilitate the expansion of the existing Canadian tire store and provide for additional site improvements.
Over the next few slides, I will walk through the proposed changes to the concept plan.

The enhancements include modifying the existing parking area to establish a strong pedestrian connection, including landscaping and resting or seating locations.

The proposed text amendments to the DCD-3 regulations contained in the zoning by-law include reducing required parking spaces from one space per 20 square meters of gross floor area to one space per 30 square meters of gross floor area for all permitted and accessory uses.
Of note, should city council adopt regulations to remove parking minimum requirements under the ongoing work associated with the housing accelerator fund.
Those amendments that are proposed today would take will be proposed will take precedent over the proposed new parking rate of one space per 30 square meters.

And clarify that the outdoor sales area does not have to be immediately adjacent to an existing large format retail store that it is associated with.
